paragraphs.english: The drama club needed a poster for its next play. Two students, Lily and Dan, offered to design it. Lily worked quickly and sent a finished poster that evening. Dan said he wanted to ask the actors about the story first. When Lily saw no reply from him the following morning, she thought he had forgotten the task. She told the club leader that she might have to do everything alone. Later that day, Dan arrived with notes from three actors and several small drawings. He had spent the evening talking to them and had planned to show his ideas at the meeting. Lily realized that she had misunderstood his silence. This made her feel embarrassed. The two students agreed to send short progress messages each evening, even when their work was not ready to show. They combined Lily's clear lettering with Dan's picture of the main character. Their final poster was better because both kinds of work had been included.
paragraphs.translation: 演劇部は次の公演のポスターを必要としていた。リリーとダンの二人が、デザインを申し出た。リリーは手早く作業し、その晩に完成したポスターを送った。ダンは、先に役者たちに物語について尋ねたいと言った。翌朝ダンの返事がないのを見ると、リリーは彼が作業を忘れたのだと思った。部長に、自分一人で全てしなければならないかもしれないと伝えた。その日の後刻、ダンは役者三人からの聞き取りメモと小さな下絵を数枚持って来た。前の晩に役者たちと話し、会議で案を示すつもりだった。ダンの沈黙を誤解していたとリリーは気づいた。そう気づいたことで、リリーは恥ずかしくなった。作業をまだ見せられなくても、毎晩短い進捗連絡を送ろうと二人は決めた。リリーの分かりやすい文字と、ダンが描いた主人公の絵を組み合わせた。両方の作業が含まれたため、最終ポスターはよりよくなった。

paragraphs.english: At a school exhibition, the science class showed models of bridges. Each model had a long card explaining its design. Younger visitors often looked at the model for a few seconds and walked away without reading. The students wanted to help these visitors understand what made each bridge different. They added short cards with a question at the top, such as Which bridge can carry the most toy cars? Below each question was a simple action that visitors could try. These were placed in front of the longer explanations. Children began testing the models, then asked to read more about the strongest designs. The students kept both kinds of card because some adults wanted detailed information from the start. At the end of the day, the class discussed what had changed. They had not made the science easier by removing important ideas. Instead, they had created a first step that gave visitors a reason to explore those ideas for themselves.
paragraphs.translation: 学校の展示会で、理科のクラスは橋の模型を展示した。各模型には、その設計を説明する長い札が付いていた。年少の来場者は、模型を数秒見て、読まずに去ることが多かった。生徒たちは、橋ごとの違いをこうした来場者に理解してもらいたかった。「どの橋が最も多くのおもちゃの車を支えられるか」など、上部に問いを載せた短い札を追加した。それぞれの問いの下には、来場者が試せる簡単な動作が書かれていた。これらの短い札は、長い解説の手前に置かれた。子供たちは模型を試し始め、その後、最も丈夫な設計をもっと読みたいと求めた。最初から詳しい情報を望む大人もいたので、両方の札を残した。一日の終わりに、クラスは何が変わったか話し合った。重要な考えを除いて、科学を簡単にしたわけではなかった。むしろ、来場者自身がその考えを探究したくなる最初の一歩を作ったのだった。

paragraphs.english: On a rainy afternoon, the library put a basket of spare umbrellas near its entrance. Visitors could borrow one and return it on another day. For the first week, almost none came back. The librarian, Ken, did not want to end the service immediately. He asked several visitors whether the return instructions were clear. One visitor said she had borrowed an umbrella but could not remember which building it belonged to. Another thought she had to return it before the library closed that same evening. Ken attached a bright label to each handle. It showed the library's name and said that umbrellas could be returned any day the library was open. He also put an empty return basket inside the door. They made the service easier to use, and more umbrellas came back the next week. Ken learned that people could want to do the right thing but still need clear information about how to do it.
paragraphs.translation: 雨の午後、図書館は入口近くに予備の傘のかごを置いた。来館者は一本借り、別の日に返せた。最初の一週間は、ほとんど返ってこなかった。司書のケンは、すぐに制度をやめたくなかった。何人かに、返却案内は分かりやすいか尋ねた。一人は、傘を借りたがどの建物の物か思い出せないと言った。別の人は、その日の閉館までに返す必要があると思っていた。ケンは持ち手ごとに目立つ札を付けた。札には図書館名と、開館日ならいつでも傘を返せるという案内があった。入口の内側には空の返却かごも置いた。札と返却かごによって利用がしやすくなり、翌週にはより多くの傘が戻った。正しいことをしたい人にも、その方法の分かりやすい情報が必要な場合があるとケンは学んだ。

title: キャンプ場からのメール

paragraphs.english: Dear members, Thank you for joining next month's weekend camp. Please read this message before packing your bags. We will meet at the east entrance of the station at eight on Saturday morning. The west entrance is closer to the shops, but our bus cannot stop there. It will leave at eight fifteen, so please call the leader if you are delayed. Bring a packed lunch for the first day. We will cook dinner together, and breakfast will be provided on Sunday. You do not need to bring a cooking pot because the campsite lends them to groups. You should bring your own cup and a small towel. The weather in the hills can change quickly. Even if the morning is sunny, keep a rain jacket in your bag. We have planned outdoor games and a short nature walk. If heavy rain makes those activities impossible, we will use the meeting hall for a map game and a craft session. Best wishes, The camp team.
paragraphs.translation: 会員の皆様、来月の週末キャンプへの参加ありがとうございます。荷造りをする前に、この連絡を読んでください。土曜朝八時に駅の東口で集合します。西口は店に近いのですが、私たちのバスはそこに停車できません。バスは八時十五分に出発するので、遅れる場合はリーダーへ電話してください。初日のお弁当を持参してください。夕食は一緒に調理し、日曜の朝食は用意されます。キャンプ場が団体に貸すので、調理鍋を持参する必要はありません。自分のカップと小さなタオルは持参してください。丘陵地の天気は急変することがあります。朝が晴れていても、かばんにレインジャケットを入れておいてください。屋外ゲームと短い自然散策を計画しています。大雨でそれらができない場合、集会所で地図ゲームと工作を行います。どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。キャンプ運営チーム。

paragraphs.english: For a local history event, Isabel interviewed her grandfather about the old railway. She brought a small digital recorder and her phone. The recorder had a new battery, while the phone was nearly out of power. Her grandfather spoke for an hour about trains that carried fruit from nearby farms. Isabel listened carefully and asked about the workers at the station. Before leaving, she checked both devices. The phone had stopped after ten minutes, but the other had recorded the whole conversation. She was glad that she had not depended on only one device. At home, she copied the recording to her computer and wrote down the parts she wanted to use. Her grandfather later helped her check the names of people and places. At the event, visitors heard short sections of his voice beside old photographs. Several said that hearing someone who had actually worked there made the railway seem more real than a list of dates alone.
paragraphs.translation: 地域の歴史行事のため、イザベルは古い鉄道について祖父に取材した。小型のデジタル録音機と携帯電話を持参した。録音機の電池は新品だった一方、携帯は電池がほとんど切れかけていた。祖父は、近隣の農場の果物を運ぶ列車について一時間話した。イザベルは注意深く聞き、駅の労働者について尋ねた。帰る前に、両方の機器を確認した。携帯は十分後に止まっていたが、もう一方は会話全体を録音できていた。一台だけに頼らずよかったと思った。家で録音をパソコンに写し、使いたい箇所を書き留めた。後に祖父は、人名と地名の確認を手伝った。行事で、来場者は古い写真の横で祖父の声の短い部分を聞いた。実際にそこで働いた人の声を聞くと、年表だけより鉄道が身近に感じられると言う人もいた。

previousSyntax.sentence: Isabel listened carefully and asked about the workers at the station.
previousSyntax.translation: イザベルは注意深く聴き駅の働き手について質問した。
previousSyntax.explanation: listenedとaskedがandで並ぶ。about以下は質問の話題。

sentences.english: For a local history event, Isabel interviewed her grandfather about the old railway.
sentences.translation: 地域の歴史行事のため、イザベルは古い鉄道について祖父に取材した。
sentences.sourceEnglish: For a local history event, Isabel interviewed her grandfather about the old railway.

sentences.english: She brought a small digital recorder and her phone.
sentences.translation: 小型のデジタル録音機と携帯電話を持参した。
sentences.sourceEnglish: She brought a small digital recorder and her phone.

sentences.english: The recorder had a new battery, while the phone was nearly out of power.
sentences.translation: 録音機の電池は新品だった一方、携帯は電池がほとんど切れかけていた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: The recorder had a new battery, while the phone was nearly out of power.

sentences.english: Her grandfather spoke for an hour about trains that carried fruit from nearby farms.
sentences.translation: 祖父は、近隣の農場の果物を運ぶ列車について一時間話した。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Her grandfather spoke for an hour about trains that carried fruit from nearby farms.

sentences.english: Isabel listened carefully and asked about the workers at the station.
sentences.translation: イザベルは注意深く聞き、駅の労働者について尋ねた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Isabel listened carefully and asked about the workers at the station.

sentences.english: Before leaving, she checked both devices.
sentences.translation: 帰る前に、両方の機器を確認した。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Before leaving, she checked both devices.

sentences.english: The phone had stopped after ten minutes, but the other had recorded the whole conversation.
sentences.translation: 携帯は十分後に止まっていたが、もう一方は会話全体を録音できていた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: The phone had stopped after ten minutes, but the other had recorded the whole conversation.

sentences.english: She was glad that she had not depended on only one device.
sentences.translation: 一台だけに頼らずよかったと思った。
sentences.sourceEnglish: She was glad that she had not depended on only one device.

sentences.english: At home, she copied the recording to her computer and wrote down the parts she wanted to use.
sentences.translation: 家で録音をパソコンに写し、使いたい箇所を書き留めた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: At home, she copied the recording to her computer and wrote down the parts she wanted to use.

sentences.english: Her grandfather later helped her check the names of people and places.
sentences.translation: 後に祖父は、人名と地名の確認を手伝った。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Her grandfather later helped her check the names of people and places.

sentences.english: At the event, visitors heard short sections of his voice beside old photographs.
sentences.translation: 行事で、来場者は古い写真の横で祖父の声の短い部分を聞いた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: At the event, visitors heard short sections of his voice beside old photographs.

sentences.english: Several said that hearing someone who had actually worked there made the railway seem more real than a list of dates alone.
sentences.translation: 実際にそこで働いた人の声を聞くと、年表だけより鉄道が身近に感じられると言う人もいた。
sentences.sourceEnglish: Several said that hearing someone who had actually worked there made the railway seem more real than a list of dates alone.
